summary:
Yoga in space.

Yoga in Space explores the potential of yoga-inspired exercise, gamification and digital technology to support human wellbeing and physical performance in space environments.

The project investigates perceived heat stress during physical activity, focusing on how individuals experience thermal discomfort, exertion and changes in comfort during exercise. This is particularly relevant to the challenges of maintaining astronaut health and wellbeing in enclosed space habitats.

Inspired by the 26 postures of Bikram Yoga, our Hot Yoga Challenge mobile application provides a digital framework for structured movement, posture tracking and exercise progression. The concept explores how self-reported thermal sensation, perceived exertion and exercise data could be combined to better understand the relationship between physical activity and perceived heat stress.

Through mobile technology i am animated the yoga sequence and space goers can view the animation on the app. It is in development.

The Hot Yoga Challenge application is available on Google Play:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.lovable.hotflowtracker

The project is part of our wider World Pilates Balls initiative, connecting movement science, space exploration and interactive fitness to investigate innovative approaches to human wellbeing and future spaceflight.

details:
YOGA IN SPACE – Exploring Perceived Heat Stress, Consistency and Human Performance

Yoga in Space explores how yoga-inspired exercise, digital technology and sports science could contribute to understanding human performance and wellbeing in space environments.

A central focus is perceived heat stress during physical activity. We want to investigate how people experience thermal discomfort, physical exertion and changes in perceived comfort during exercise, particularly in enclosed and thermally challenging environments relevant to future space habitats.

The project builds on the 26 postures and 2 breathing exercises of traditional Bikram Yoga. Through our Hot Yoga Challenge mobile application, users can follow structured exercise sessions, develop consistency through daily practice and 30-day challenges, track their progress and share their achievements with others.

An important research dimension is the relationship between perceived thermal sensation, perceived exertion and physical activity. By combining subjective user feedback with exercise and movement data, we aim to explore how sports science methods could help investigate individual responses to heat and physical stress.

The project also explores AI-assisted animation, 3D motion capture and computer vision to visualise and analyse human movement.

We are particularly interested in the research of Marco L. Della Vedova at Chalmers University of Technology, whose work explores applied AI, spatial intelligence, orienteering and the analysis of human decision-making during physical activity. His research provides an interesting inspiration for future exploration of AI-assisted movement analysis and performance tracking.

Our wider World Pilates Balls vision is to connect fitness, sports science, artificial intelligence and space exploration, creating engaging ways to encourage consistent exercise and investigate human performance both on Earth and potentially beyond it.
